newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian ministers to discuss tense Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russian ministers to discuss tense Chechnya.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will meet top ministers and Kremlin security chief Alexander Lebed on Saturday to discuss efforts to seal the peace in breakaway Chechnya, where tension remains high.

Russian news agencies on Friday quoted sources close to the prime minister as saying Chernomyrdin had convened the "power ministers" -- including defence and interior -- to discuss the peace deal Lebed reached with the region's separatist rebels.

On Friday, Russian army commanders in the region said they were still holding up troop withdrawals because of disputes with the separatist rebels over the exchange of prisoners. The pullout began last weekend and was halted almost immediately.
The general in charge of Russian interior troops said 12 of his men had been killed since a ceasefire on August 23. He accused the rebels of continuing to concentrate their forces.
Separatist spokesman Movladi Udugov hit back, accusing the Russians of transferring Chechen captives to criminal jails as a way of avoiding freeing them as prisoners of war.
Chechen chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov, who signed the deal with Lebed, told Interfax news agency: "This is yet more senseless brinkmanship, which could mean new casualties."
"The Chechen side is ready for any eventuality," he added.

Doku Zavgayev, the head of the Moscow-backed Chechen government who was left out in the cold by Lebed's August 31 deal with Maskhadov, had to deny rumours that forces loyal to his administration were about to attack the capital Grozny.
Local residents said a considerable number of local people, who had already fled their homes in the half-ruined city when the separatists attacked six weeks ago, were leaving town.
Grozny is being policed and defended by joint patrols of separatist guerrillas and Russian forces.

Zavgayev boycotted the first attempt this week to convene a multi-party Chechen assembly although he later said he would listen to Lebed's call for him to help form a coalition government with the separatists led by Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev.

President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday handed responsibility for the "power ministries" to Chernomyrdin as he prepared for heart surgery. In his absence speculation is rife that Lebed, who reports to Yeltsin, and Chernomyrdin are vying for power.

Chernomyrdin grudgingly approved the deal Lebed struck on August 31 following the rebels' seizure of the capital Grozny. Under it, Moscow is to pull out its troops while the separatists agreed to defer the key question of secession for five years.
The prime minister said on Friday that Lebed's agreement "had several differences" from the text which had been approved in advance by the Russian Security Council.
